newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends firm in shortcovering rally.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends firm in shortcovering rally.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled mostly firmer and just shy of session highs in a shortcovering rally, traders said.
"I'd say once it became clear we weren't going to test support, we started to see some short-covering come in from locals and commission houses," a trader said.
Traders also said nearby wheat contracts drew strength from commercial bull-spreading, with Cargill Inc and Continental both appearing on the buy side of spread trades.
Wheat saw limited strength as wet fields disrupted harvest progress in central Texas.
Traders said they had seen players buying KCBT July and selling CBOT July on the intermarket spread amid ideas that HRW wheat values had dropped to a level that may encourage export sales.
KCBT wheat settled nine cents lower to 6-1/4 cents higher, with July up 6-1/4 cents at $3.83 a bushel. September gained five cents to close at $3.85.

Wolcott Lincoln bought 3.6 million July bushels and Refco picked up 1.1 million July and 2.2 million September. CIS bull-spread 1.2 million July/Sept at two cents, and Continental Grain bull-spread 1.5 million July/December at nine cents.
